Megan/Monica —

Short technical summary on KMS and EdgeCache access. Happy to expand on any point on a call.

1) Key custody model
- Redwood supports two deployment surfaces: 
  a) Customer-managed KMS: customers can supply keys via our integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an enterprise HSM endpoint. In this mode we never persist plaintext customer root keys in our control plane; keys are invoked via KMS API calls and are never exported.
  b) Redwood-managed KMS: for self-hosted tenants or early-stage customers we may provision keys in cloud-managed KMS (our tenant-specific key rings). In those cases keys are held in provider-managed HSMs (AWS/GCP) and access is restricted to our control plane services using least-privileged roles and audited via key usage logs.

2) EdgeCache Inc. (subprocessor)
- Function: lightweight KV prefix cache for repeated prompt prefixes and session state (cache hit rate improves token-level latency).
- Data access: EdgeCache is deployed with encryption-at-rest and in-transit; they do NOT receive customer KMS root keys.
- Operationally: the KV entries stored on EdgeCache are encrypted by per-tenant data encryption keys (DEKs) that are provisioned by our runtime and rotated; EdgeCache only stores the ciphertext and does not have the KMS ability to decrypt or request plaintext. Decryption occurs inside our runtime binders that hold the ephemeral DEK in memory for the duration of a request.

3) Telemetry and logs
- Traces and metric samples are redacted by default — no plaintext prompt content is stored in telemetry. Any customer-configured telemetry capture that includes prompt content must be explicitly enabled by the customer and we document that in onboarding.

4) Evidence we can provide by 2026-02-10
- Subprocessor roster CSV with residency columns (attached by Monica).
- A 1-page KMS provenance summary (I will attach).
- Redacted HSM attestation from our upstream cloud provider (we can provide a redacted export of the HSM ARN and signature metadata).

If you need cryptographic proofs (e.g., KMIP manifests or HSM certs), we'll need a short POA and CA to share sensitive vendor attestations; Marissa can coordinate.

Ben Carter
Sr. Platform Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

• Can you explicitly confirm whether the DEK rotation and the KMS API calls happen entirely within your runtime process (i.e., are the DEKs ever staged or cached on the EdgeCache nodes in decrypted form)?

Also — HealthCore's procurement team wants to add a short addendum to our master SaaS agreement to require redacted HSM attestations for any subprocessor that touches encrypted customer data. Is that something Redwood can accept as a limited-scope addendum?

Megan —

Attached are the artifacts we discussed. Summary and next steps below.

Attachments included:
- subprocessors_inventory_20260203.csv — roster with columns: service, role, residency, data_types_processed, kms_custody (yes/no), notes.
- kms_provenance_summary_20260210.pdf — 1-page summary describing customer-managed vs Redwood-managed KMS flows, HSM custody, and rotation cadence.
- sig-lite_answer_matrix_HealthCore.xlsx — our SIG-lite exports with the fields you flagged highlighted.

Key confirmations (written):
- EdgeCache Inc. never receives plaintext DEKs or customer root KMS keys. DEKs are generated per-tenant in the runtime and only exist in memory during request processing. We do not persist DEKs on EdgeCache nodes.
- For Redwood-managed KMS, key usage logs are available and we can provide timestamped key usage records scoped to your tenant for the period requested; those logs are generated by the cloud KMS and exported to our audit pipeline.
- We can provide a redacted HSM attestation from our cloud provider that includes the HSM identifier and signing hash; we will redact provider-internal IPs and account names. To share the full attestation (unredacted) we require an executed NDA addendum — Marissa can coordinate.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm receipt and if the redaction level is acceptable.
2) If you want the unredacted attestation, reply with a POA or Marissa will share a template NDA addendum for signature.
3) If helpful, Ben and I can do a 30-minute technical walkthrough next week — propose times and we'll lock it in.

Thanks — hope this closes your panel questions.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
